title: Mercy and Forgiveness
blurb: Walk from David's prayer of repentance through the prophets and parables to the Cross, where mercy is shown at its fullest.

steps.title: The Lord, merciful and gracious
steps.intro: After the golden calf, God passes before Moses and proclaims his own name: merciful and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in steadfast love. All the later Scripture on mercy returns to this declaration.

quote.text: O great is Thy patience, Lord, full of compassion and gracious, slow to anger, and plenteous in mercy, and true;

steps.question: Which word in this description of God do you find hardest to believe about him?

steps.title: Have mercy on me, O God
steps.intro: Psalm 51 is the prayer traditionally attributed to David after his sin with Bathsheba. It asks for mercy, a clean heart and a renewed spirit, and has long been the Church's model prayer of repentance.

quote.text: If in doing sin thou sayest thou hast done nothing, thou wilt be nothing, thou wilt receive nothing: God is ready to give indulgence, thou closest the door against thyself: He is ready to give, do not oppose the bar of defence, but open the bosom of confession.

steps.question: What would it cost you to name your failure plainly to God, without excuses?

steps.title: How can I give you up?
steps.intro: Hosea portrays God as a parent who taught Israel to walk and was repaid with rebellion. Yet his heart recoils at the thought of abandoning his child, and he chooses compassion over wrath.

quote.text: What mark of His mercy have we more ready at hand than that He Himself, through the prophet Hosea, is at once merciful as though reconciled to those whom in His anger He had threatened?

steps.question: What does it mean for you that God's compassion is described as stronger than his anger?

steps.title: The father runs to meet him
steps.intro: A younger son wastes his inheritance and returns in shame. His father sees him from a long way off, runs to embrace him and restores him to the family with a feast.

quote.text: No difference was made between the son who had never left his father, and his brother who was welcomed as a returning penitent.

steps.question: Which son do you most resemble right now, and what would it mean to come home?

steps.title: Neither do I condemn you
steps.intro: Some scribes and Pharisees bring Jesus a woman accused of adultery and ask what should be done. He invites the one without sin to throw the first stone. When her accusers leave, he tells her, 'Neither do I condemn you; go, and do not sin again.'

quote.text: But they, turning their thought to themselves, and by that very withdrawal having confessed concerning themselves, had left the woman with her great sin to Him who was without sin.

steps.question: When have you been quick to judge, and what might Jesus be inviting you to put down instead?

steps.title: The servant who would not forgive
steps.intro: Peter asks how often he must forgive, and Jesus tells of a servant forgiven an enormous debt who refuses to forgive a small one. The parable shows that mercy received is meant to be mercy given.

quote.text: For that sins which have been remitted do return upon a man, where there is no brotherly love, is most clearly taught by our Lord, in the case of the servant whom He found owing Him ten thousand talents, and to whom He yet forgave all at his entreaty.

steps.question: What small debt is someone else holding in your mind, in light of the much larger one forgiven you?

steps.title: Father, forgive them
steps.intro: Crucified between two criminals, Jesus asks the Father to forgive those who are killing him. He also promises Paradise to the repentant man beside him.

quote.text: For pitying the misery of them even while hanging on the Cross, He saith, “Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do.”

steps.question: Who is hardest for you to forgive, and could you begin by praying for them?
